title: What did we learn on our journey through big numbers?
description: A numbered board of the six ideas of the chapter: ten thousand, reading, comparing, rounding, journeys, and puzzles, then one question to try.
teaching_notes: Six ideas, one line each, nothing new. The closing question is rounding to the nearest hundred; watch for children who always round up.

source: What we learned in We the Travellers - I
video_script.why: The child has met all the ideas of the chapter and now needs them together on one board before moving on.
video_script.substitution: Say each idea in one line, then ask one rounding question with new numbers.
video_script.anchor: a numbered board of the six ideas of the chapter, drawn like a train route with six stops
maths_rules: 10 thousands = 10,000, which needs a new TTh column
5-digit numbers are read from the thousands part, with commas and number names
compare: count the digits first; with equal digits compare from the left
round to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand: pick the neighbour with the fewest jumps
distance = distance in one hour x number of hours; vehicles needed = people divided by seats
pebble game: take the same number from the other pile (mirroring); a corner horse is counted on two sides, so take away 1
your turn: 6,284 lies between 6,200 and 6,300; 84 is more than 50, so it is nearer 6,300; answer 6,300; never shown
video_script.design: Six numbered lines on a train route board, one idea each, then one rounding question with new numbers. Nothing new is taught.

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Idea one is that ten thousand is ten thousands, and it needs a new column.
<bookmark mark='left'/>That column sits to the left of the thousands.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Idea two is that five digit numbers are read from the thousands part first. We then write them with commas and number names.

beats.on_screen: stop 3 reads count the digits first, then compare from the left; stop 4 reads round to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand; the fewest jumps is circled

marks.three: stop 3 reads count the digits first, then compare from the left
marks.left: an arrow runs from the left digit across the number
marks.four: stop 4 reads round to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Idea three is to compare numbers by counting the digits first. With equal digits, compare from the left.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Compare each place from the left, and stop at the first place that differs.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Idea four is rounding to the nearest ten, hundred or thousand.
<bookmark mark='jumps'/>Pick the neighbour that needs the fewest jumps.

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Idea five is that distance in many hours is the distance in one hour times the hours.
<bookmark mark='cars'/>Vehicles needed come from dividing the people by the seats.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Idea six is that puzzles teach us to think with a plan.
<bookmark mark='mirror'/>In the pebble game, mirroring means taking the same number from the other pile.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>A corner horse is counted on two sides, so we take away one.
